newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BRAZILIANS FANS ALREADY CATCHING WORLD CUP FEVER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZILIANS FANS ALREADY CATCHING WORLD CUP FEVER.

text.p: Brazilian soccer fans have applied for 120,000 tickets for the opening match of the World Cup finals next year -- even though they don't yet know who their team will be playing.

In any case, the venue for the match, the new Stade de France, will have a capacity of only 80,000 and with many of those tickets going to French fans and the fans of Brazil's opposition, many Brazilian fans are in for a major disappointment.
According to EDS, an official service provider for the finals, more than one million tickets have already been sold for the first round of the tournament since going on sale on November 27 last year.
Michel Platini, co-president of the French Organising Committee (CFO) said on Tuesday that 1.2 million tickets had already been sold for the whole tournament which runs from June 10 to July 12, 1998.
EDS spokesman Gerard Gouillou said on Tuesday: "The tickets sold to date through official outlets have been for stadiums where construction is yet to be completed.
"Once paid for, the purchaser is sent a receipt confirming the sale and becomes a fan in a "virtual stadium".
Seats will not actually be designated until next February or March when construction work is due to be completed in all 10 stadiums.
In an attempt to reduce the possibility of fraud, organisers of France '98 are handling the design and distribution of the tickets from France.
Fans who buy a ticket for the finals will have their details logged and no ticket agencies will be involved in selling the tickets, which will all be done by the central organising office.
Of the 2.5 million tickets available for France '98, 60 percent are expected to go to the French public.
Ticket prices range from between 145 ($29) and 350 francs ($70) for a first round match to 350 to 2,950 francs ($590) for the final.
